breadcrumb: Floor graphics with a defined purpose
h1: Floor graphics with a defined purpose
lead: Floor graphics put a message into the path people use, which makes placement and material suitability essential. They can support a temporary promotion, reinforce a route or mark an approved waiting area, but the floor is a working surface with its own cleaning and wear conditions. Vision Graphics can help New York businesses plan the message and visual layout for review. Share the flooring type, traffic pattern and intended display period so the selected product can be assessed for that specific use.

sections.html: People tend to encounter a floor message while moving. Use a simple visual, limited text and a clear direction when needed. Place graphics where they can be seen without creating confusing paths or competing with essential building signs.

sections.h2: Review the surface and material documentation
sections.html: Identify the floor finish, texture, cleaning method and areas exposed to moisture. The proposed material should have documentation appropriate to the application, including any relevant slip-related performance. Testing, preparation and removal requirements need review before production and placement.

items.p: Connect a focused campaign message to an approved interior location.
Use arrows or markers as part of a coordinated route.
Organize approved waiting or service positions with clear graphics.

items.q: Can floor graphics go on any flooring?
items.a_html: No. The floor, exposure, cleaning and material documentation must be reviewed for compatibility and suitability.

items.q: Are floor graphics automatically slip resistant?
items.a_html: No general assurance is made here. Review the specific product’s documented performance and the actual use conditions.
